text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTaiwan(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
HoldTaiwanese(x) ::: x holds Taiwanese citizenship.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina.
Gazprom ::: Gazprom.

Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote can participate.
CitizenshipUS(x) → CanRegister(x) ::: If someone has US citizenship, they can register.
Citizenship(x) ∨ Citizenship(y) ::: A person either has US or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldTaiwanese(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir does not hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldTaiwanese(Vladimir) ∧ ¬Manager(Vladimir, Gazprom) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegister(Ekaterina) ∨ Official(Ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register or is an official.

Conclusion:
¬Official(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir is not a Russian Federation official.
